haiku-low.q1: They sign in to the same account. Google's sub is the key, and a linked sub signs in regardless of email changes; Google's email is ignored.
haiku-low.q2: The user must enter that account's correct password on the password form. Only then is the Google sub linked and a session started.
haiku-low.q3: Each wrong password adds 1 to failed_logins and keeps the pending link. On the fifth, the account locks for 15 minutes, failed_logins resets, and the pending link is deleted.
haiku-low.q4: No match: one transaction creates a password-less verified user and the link, then a session starts. Unverified: refused, nothing created, user pointed to email and password.
haiku-low.q5: Twelve minutes exceeds the 600-second attempt TTL, so the callback gets the error page and nothing changes. A repeated callback also fails, since GETDEL already spent the attempt.
haiku-low.q6: A new sessions row and sid cookie, via the same start_session used by password login. An older sessions row the browser had is deleted first.
haiku-low.q7: Only a valid session is needed; no password or email match. If the sub is linked to another user, it is refused as account in use and nothing changes.
haiku-low.q8: In Redis under key oidc:{state}, with the state cookie in the browser. GETDEL at callback removes the attempt; expiry after 600 seconds also removes it.
haiku-low.q9: In Redis under pending:{id}, holding sub, target user, origin and next. The browser refers to it by the pending cookie. Success, lock, link conflict or expiry deletes it; a wrong password keeps it.
haiku-low.q10: In the PostgreSQL table google_identities. sub is its primary key (one Google account, one user) and user_id is UNIQUE (one user, one Google account).
haiku-low.q11: Failed code exchange: origin page with a neutral try-again message, and the code is never retried. Invalid ID token: an error page. Both spend the attempt.
haiku-low.q12: The attempt's stored origin (login or settings) tells the callback which flow it is. For settings, it checks the session is valid and its user_id matches the attempt's user_id.

sonnet.q1: Sign-in works: if sub is in google_identities, the linked user is signed in; Google's email and email_verified are ignored, so the email change doesn't matter and they reach the same account (then start_session).
sonnet.q2: The password must be confirmed first. The server creates a pending link in Redis and shows a password form for that account (no session yet). Only after the bcrypt password matches does it insert the google_identities row in a transaction, delete the pending link, and call start_session. (Also U must not already have a different Google account, and U must not be locked.)
sonnet.q3: Each wrong password adds 1 to failed_logins and the pending link is kept (until its 10-minute TTL) so the user can retry. At the 5th failure, locked_until is set to now + 15 minutes, failed_logins reset to 0, the pending link is deleted (link discarded, nothing linked), and the locked message is shown. If already locked, the password isn't checked and the pending is deleted.
sonnet.q4: Verified email with no matching user: in one transaction create a users row (password_hash NULL, email_verified_at now) plus a google_identities row, then start a session. If email_verified is false: refuse, point user to email and password sign-in; nothing is created.
sonnet.q5: Error page, nothing changes. Expired (after 600 s TTL) or reused states get the same error page. A second load fails because GETDEL spent the attempt.
sonnet.q6: The normal session: start_session(user_id) inserts a sessions row and sets the sid cookie (no new session type). It deletes the old sid sessions row if the browser had one, inserts a new row, sets sid, and clears the state/pending/oidc cookies.
sonnet.q7: Neither a password nor an email match is required (email match explicitly not required), but a valid session is needed and email_verified must be true. If the sub is already linked to another user, it is refused (account in use) and nothing changes. (If linked to this user: shows already linked.)
sonnet.q8: In a Redis attempt record at key oidc:{state} (state, nonce, code verifier, origin, next, user id for settings), TTL 600 s; the state is also set in a browser cookie. Removed by GETDEL at the callback, or by expiry. The state cookie is cleared at callback or expires.
sonnet.q9: In Redis key pending:{id} holding sub, target user id U, origin and next, TTL 600 s. The browser refers to it via a pending cookie (HttpOnly, Secure, SameSite=Lax, same lifetime) that must match. Deleted on success, on lock (5th failure or already locked), on link conflict, or by expiry; kept after a wrong password.
sonnet.q10: In the PostgreSQL table google_identities (sub, user_id, linked_at). sub is PRIMARY KEY (one Google account links to at most one user) and user_id is NOT NULL UNIQUE with FK to users ON DELETE CASCADE (one Google account per user).
sonnet.q11: Code exchange failure (network, timeout, non-200): redirected to the origin page with a neutral try again message; the code is never retried, user starts again. Invalid ID token: error page. In both cases the attempt is spent and nothing changes.
sonnet.q12: By the origin stored in the attempt record (login vs settings), read at the callback. For settings, the attempt stores the user_id from the session; at the callback the server checks the session is still valid and its user_id equals the attempt's user_id, else redirects to login with a neutral message and nothing changes.
